turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes, Hale. Owen's zero comes off the gradebook, and I want to know why nobody called me before it went in.
"You need an answer today." I asked you one first, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Either Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript.

"Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM, or the zero goes on his transcript." I'm writing that down, and I'll want it in an email. What do you actually have, Hale, because so far I've heard a deadline and no document.
Those are the only two options. Pick one.
Neither. Your own procedure says a parent is called before any mark goes in, and nobody called me. Then I'm going upstairs to the principal, unless you have a document to put in front of me.
